    /// Raw payload.
    Raw(Vec<u8>),
}

/// A single frame statement inside a flow.
///
/// Syntax mapping:
/// ```frameassembly
/// client -> server TCP SYN ACK PAYLOAD "World" WAIT 10ms
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FrameStatement<'a> {
    /// The caller (source) identifier with span.
    pub caller: Spanned<&'a str>,
    /// The direction of the packet.
    pub dir: Direction,
    /// Alias for direction matching the layered contract.
    pub arrow: ArrowDirection,
    /// The callee (destination) identifier with span.
    pub callee: Spanned<&'a str>,
    /// The protocol used.
    pub protocol: Protocol,
    /// Optional protocol-specific scoped details.
    pub protocol_spec: Option<ProtocolSpec<'a>>,
    /// Layer 2 modifiers.
    pub l2: L2Modifiers,
    /// Layer 3 modifiers.
    pub l3: L3Modifiers,
    /// Layer 4 modifiers.
    pub l4: L4Modifiers,
    /// Optional string payload.
    pub payload: Option<String>,
    /// Optional raw binary hex payload.
    pub hex_payload: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    /// Optional wait time before sending the packet (in nanoseconds).
    pub wait: Option<u64>,
    /// Source span of this statement.
    pub span: (usize, usize),
    /// Raw parsed VLAN ID and span for semantic range validation.
    pub raw_vlan: Option<(u32, (usize, usize))>,
    /// Raw parsed DSCP and span for semantic range validation.
    pub raw_dscp: Option<(u32, (usize, usize))>,
    /// Raw parsed ECN and span for semantic range validation.
    pub raw_ecn: Option<(u32, (usize, usize))>,
    /// Raw parsed TTL and span for semantic range validation.
    pub raw_ttl: Option<(u32, (usize, usize))>,
    /// Raw parsed FLOWLABEL and span for semantic range validation.
    pub raw_flowlabel: Option<(u32, (usize, usize))>,
    /// Raw parsed GENTRAP span for semantic range validation.
    pub raw_gentrap_span: Option<(usize, usize)>,
    /// Any duplicate statement modifiers detected during parsing.
    pub duplicate_modifiers: Vec<(String, (usize, usize))>,

    // Flat compatibility fields for snmp_builder and backend
    /// Optional source port.
    pub src_port: Option<u16>,
    /// Optional destination port.
    pub dst_port: Option<u16>,
    /// TCP flags.
    pub flags: Vec<TcpFlag>,
    /// Optional TCP sequence number.
    pub seq: Option<u32>,
    /// Optional TCP acknowledgment number.
    pub ack_num: Option<u32>,
    /// Optional TCP window size.
    pub win: Option<u16>,
    /// Optional TCP urgent pointer.
    pub urgent: Option<u16>,
    /// Optional SNMP community string.
    pub community: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Optional SNMP user.
    pub user: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Optional SNMP OID.
    pub oid: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Optional SNMP system uptime.
    pub sys_up_time: Option<u32>,
    /// PDU Type.
    pub pdu_type: Option<SnmpPduType>,
    /// Optional enterprise OID for v1 traps.
    pub enterprise: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Optional agent IP for v1 traps.
    pub agent_ip: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Optional generic trap for v1 traps.
    pub gen_trap: Option<u32>,
    /// Optional specific trap for v1 traps.
    pub spec_trap: Option<u32>,
    /// Optional engine ID for v3.
    pub engine_id: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Optional engine boots for v3.
    pub engine_boots: Option<u32>,
    /// Optional engine time for v3.
    pub engine_time: Option<u32>,
    /// Optional context name for v3.
    pub context_name: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Optional auth params for v3.
    pub auth: Option<(SnmpAuthType, &'a str)>,
    /// Optional priv params for v3.
    pub priv_param: Option<(SnmpPrivType, &'a str)>,
    /// List of variable bindings.
    pub varbinds: Vec<VarBindAst<'a>>,
    /// Optional Non-Repeaters for GETBULK.
    pub non_repeaters: Option<u32>,
    /// Optional Max-Repetitions for GETBULK.
    pub max_repetitions: Option<u32>,
    /// Optional Request ID.
    pub req_id: Option<u32>,
}

impl<'a> FrameStatement<'a> {
    /// Returns the effective payload bytes for this frame statement.
    ///
    /// Prioritizes `hex_payload` if present, falling back to UTF-8 bytes of `payload`.
    pub fn effective_payload(&self) -> Option<&[u8]> {
        if let Some(ref hex) = self.hex_payload {
            Some(hex.as_slice())
        } else {
            self.payload.as_deref().map(|s| s.as_bytes())
        }
    }
}

/// A flow definition in the form `FLOW name(arg1, arg2) { statements }`
///
/// Syntax mapping:
/// ```frameassembly
/// FLOW name(arg1, arg2) {
///     arg1 -> arg2 TCP SYN
/// }
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FlowDef<'a> {
    /// The name of the flow.
    pub name: &'a str,
    /// The parameters of the flow.
    pub params: Vec<&'a str>,
    /// The statements inside the flow.
    pub statements: Vec<FrameStatement<'a>>,
    /// Source span of this flow definition.
    pub span: (usize, usize),
}

/// An argument passed to a flow invocation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Argument<'a> {
    /// A simple variable reference, e.g., `my_client`
    Variable(&'a str),
}

/// A flow invocation, e.g., `tcp_handshake(my_client, google_dns)`
///
/// # Examples
/// ```
/// use frameassembly::ast::{TemplateInvocation, Argument};
/// let inv = TemplateInvocation { name: "handshake", args: vec![], span: (0, 0) };
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TemplateInvocation<'a> {
    /// The name of the flow being invoked.
    pub name: &'a str,
    /// The arguments passed to the flow.
    pub args: Vec<Argument<'a>>,
    /// Source span of the invocation.
    pub span: (usize, usize),
}

/// A statement in the run/compile block, can be a loop or a single invocation
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RunStatement<'a> {
    /// A single template invocation directly in the block
    Invocation(TemplateInvocation<'a>),
    /// A loop block containing a count and inner invocations
    Loop(u32, Vec<TemplateInvocation<'a>>),
}

/// The root of the AST containing all assignments, flows, and the compile block.
///
/// # Examples
/// ```
/// use frameassembly::ast::Program;
/// let prog = Program { hosts: vec![], flows: vec![], compile_block: vec![] };
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Program<'a> {
    /// The list of host definitions.
    pub hosts: Vec<HostDef<'a>>,
    /// The list of flow definitions.
    pub flows: Vec<FlowDef<'a>>,
    /// The list of statements in the compile block.
    pub compile_block: Vec<RunStatement<'a>>,
}
```

// File: src/ast/l2/arp.rs
//! Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) AST definitions.

use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::net::IpAddr;

/// ARP operation code.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ArpOpcode {
    /// ARP Request (1)
    Request,
    /// ARP Reply (2)
    Reply,
}

/// Address Resolution Protocol (RFC 826) specification.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct ArpSpec<'a> {
    /// Operation code (Request or Reply).
    pub opcode: Option<ArpOpcode>,
    /// Gratuitous ARP flag.
    pub is_gratuitous: bool,
    /// Sender Hardware Address override.

    /// Sender Protocol Address override.
    pub spa: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Target Hardware Address override.
    pub tha: Option<[u8; 6]>,
    /// Target Protocol Address override.
    pub tpa: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Optional phantom reference.
    pub _marker: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}

//! Routing Information Protocol (RIP) AST definitions.

use core::marker::PhantomData;
use core::net::IpAddr;

/// RIP command.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RipCommand {
    /// Request (1)
    Request,
    /// Response (2)
    Response,
}

/// Routing Information Protocol (RFC 2453 / 2080) specification.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct RipSpec<'a> {
    /// Command (Request or Response).
    pub command: Option<RipCommand>,
    /// Route prefix IP.
    pub prefix: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Metric (hop count).
    pub metric: Option<u32>,
    /// Next Hop IP.
    pub nexthop: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Route Tag.
    pub tag: Option<u16>,
    /// Optional phantom reference.
    pub _marker: PhantomData<&'a ()>,
}

use core::marker::PhantomData;

/// WireGuard packet type.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WireguardType {
    /// Handshake Initiation (1)
    Initiation,
    /// Handshake Response (2)
    Response,
    /// Cookie Reply (3)
    Cookie,
    /// Transport Data (4)
    Data,
}

    pub counter: Option<u64>,
    /// Optional phantom reference.

}

// File: src/ast/l4/mod.rs
//! Layer 4 Transport layer protocols, TCP flags, options, and modifiers.

use alloc::vec::Vec;

/// Stream Control Transmission Protocol.
pub mod sctp;
/// Transmission Control Protocol.
pub mod tcp;
/// User Datagram Protocol.
pub mod udp;

pub use sctp::*;
pub use tcp::*;
pub use udp::*;

/// Transport layer protocol selector.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TransportProto {
    /// Transmission Control Protocol.
    Tcp,
    /// User Datagram Protocol.
    Udp,
}

/// Layer 4 transport modifiers.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct L4Modifiers {
    /// Explicit source port override.
    pub src_port: Option<u16>,
    /// Explicit destination port override.
    pub dst_port: Option<u16>,
    /// Explicit transport protocol override.
    pub transport: Option<TransportProto>,
    /// TCP flags.
    pub tcp_flags: Vec<TcpFlag>,
    /// Optional TCP urgent pointer.
    pub urgent: Option<u16>,
    /// Optional TCP options.
    pub tcp_options: Option<TcpOptions>,
    /// Optional SCTP parameters.
    pub sctp_params: Option<SctpParams>,
}

// File: src/ast/l4/sctp.rs
//! Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) AST definitions.

use alloc::string::String;

/// SCTP transport parameters override.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct SctpParams {
    /// Verification Tag.
    pub vtag: Option<u32>,
    /// Stream Identifier.
    pub stream: Option<u16>,
    /// Stream Sequence Number.
    pub ssn: Option<u16>,
    /// Payload Protocol Identifier.
    pub ppid: Option<u32>,

    pub chunk: Option<String>,
}

// File: src/ast/l4/tcp.rs
//! Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) AST definitions.

/// Represents a TCP flag.
///
/// # Examples
/// ```
/// use frameassembly::ast::TcpFlag;
/// let flag = TcpFlag::Syn;
/// ```
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum TcpFlag {
    /// SYN flag
    Syn,
    /// ACK flag
    Ack,
    /// FIN flag
    Fin,
    /// RST flag
    Rst,
    /// PSH flag
    Psh,
    /// URG flag
    Urg,
    /// ECE flag
    Ece,
    /// CWR flag
    Cwr,
}

/// TCP header options overrides.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct TcpOptions {
    /// Maximum Segment Size option.
    pub mss: Option<u16>,
    /// Window Scale option.
    pub wscale: Option<u8>,
    /// SACK Permitted option.
    pub sack_perm: bool,
    /// Timestamp Value option.
    pub tsval: Option<u32>,
    /// Timestamp Echo Reply option.
    pub tsecr: Option<u32>,
}

// File: src/ast/l7/snmp.rs
//! SNMP protocol specifications (v1, v2c, v3), PDU types, security parameters, and variable bindings.

use alloc::vec::Vec;
use core::net::IpAddr;

/// Represents the type of SNMP PDU.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SnmpPduType {
    /// Trap PDU
    Trap,
    /// GetRequest PDU
    Get,
    /// SetRequest PDU
    Set,
    /// Response PDU
    Response,
    /// InformRequest PDU
    Inform,
    /// GetNextRequest PDU
    GetNext,
    /// GetBulkRequest PDU
    GetBulk,
}

/// Represents the SNMP Auth type.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SnmpAuthType {
    /// HMAC-MD5-96
    Md5,
    /// HMAC-SHA-96
    Sha,
    /// HMAC-SHA-256
    Sha256,
    /// HMAC-SHA-384
    Sha384,
    /// HMAC-SHA-512
    Sha512,
}

/// Represents the SNMP Priv type.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SnmpPrivType {
    /// DES privacy
    Des,
    /// AES privacy
    Aes,
}

/// Represents the value of a VarBind.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum VarBindType<'a> {
    /// Null value
    Null,
    /// OctetString value
    String(&'a str),
    /// Signed 32-bit integer value
    Int(i32),
    /// TimeTicks value
    TimeTicks(u32),
    /// IpAddress value
    Ip(IpAddr),
    /// Object Identifier value
    OidVal(&'a str),
    /// 32-bit Counter value
    Counter32(u32),
    /// 32-bit Gauge value
    Gauge32(u32),
    /// 64-bit Counter value
    Counter64(u64),
}

/// Represents a single VarBind.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VarBindAst<'a> {
    /// The Object Identifier
    pub oid: &'a str,
    /// The value associated with the OID
    pub val: VarBindType<'a>,
}

/// SNMPv1-specific parameters.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Snmp1Spec<'a> {
    /// Community string.
    pub community: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Enterprise OID.
    pub enterprise: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Agent IP address.
    pub agent_ip: Option<IpAddr>,
    /// Generic trap code.
    pub gen_trap: Option<u32>,
    /// Specific trap code.
    pub spec_trap: Option<u32>,
    /// System uptime.
    pub sys_up_time: Option<u32>,
    /// List of variable bindings.
    pub varbinds: Vec<VarBindAst<'a>>,
    /// PDU Type.
    pub pdu_type: Option<SnmpPduType>,
}

/// SNMPv2c-specific parameters.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Snmp2Spec<'a> {
    /// Community string.
    pub community: Option<&'a str>,
    /// List of variable bindings.
    pub varbinds: Vec<VarBindAst<'a>>,
    /// PDU Type.
    pub pdu_type: Option<SnmpPduType>,
    /// Non-Repeaters for GETBULK.
    pub non_repeaters: Option<u32>,
    /// Max-Repetitions for GETBULK.
    pub max_repetitions: Option<u32>,
    /// Request ID.
    pub req_id: Option<u32>,
}

/// SNMPv3-specific parameters.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub struct Snmp3Spec<'a> {
    /// User name.
    pub user: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Authoritative engine ID.
    pub engine_id: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Authoritative engine boot count.
    pub engine_boots: Option<u32>,
    /// Authoritative engine time.
    pub engine_time: Option<u32>,
    /// Context name.
    pub context_name: Option<&'a str>,
    /// Authentication protocol and password.
    pub auth: Option<(SnmpAuthType, &'a str)>,
    /// Privacy protocol and password.
    pub priv_param: Option<(SnmpPrivType, &'a str)>,
    /// List of variable bindings.
    pub varbinds: Vec<VarBindAst<'a>>,
    /// PDU Type.
    pub pdu_type: Option<SnmpPduType>,
    /// Non-Repeaters for GETBULK.
    pub non_repeaters: Option<u32>,
    /// Max-Repetitions for GETBULK.
    pub max_repetitions: Option<u32>,
    /// Request ID.
    pub req_id: Option<u32>,
}

/// Type alias for SNMP variable binding.
pub type SnmpVarBind<'a> = VarBindAst<'a>;

/// Type alias for SNMP variable binding value.
pub type SnmpValue<'a> = VarBindType<'a>;

/// Type alias for SNMP authentication protocol.
pub type SnmpAuthProtocol = SnmpAuthType;

/// Type alias for SNMP privacy protocol.
pub type SnmpPrivProtocol = SnmpPrivType;

/// SNMP security model (RFC 3411 / RFC 3414).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SnmpSecurityModel {
    /// User-Based Security Model (USM, RFC 3414).
    Usm,
}

## Demonstration Example (`demo.fasm`)

```fasm
// Written vertically -> Intuitive for programmers
HOST example_server { 
    IP 10.0.10.5
    MAC aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff 
}

// Written horizontally -> Intuitive for network engineers
HOST example_nms { IP 10.0.10.100  MAC ff:ee:dd:cc:bb:aa }

// A broadcast can be declard like an ordinary host
HOST broadcast { IP 255.255.255.255  }

FLOW tcp_handshake(client, server) {
    client -> server TCP SYN PAYLOAD "Hello" SRCPORT 67 DSTPORT 100
    client <- server TCP SYN ACK PAYLOAD "World"
    client -> server TCP ACK PAYLOAD "!" 
}

FLOW snmp_v1_trap(agent, nms) {
    agent -> nms SNMP1 TRAP COMMUNITY "public" OID "1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.2"
}

FLOW snmp_v2_trap(agent, nms) {
    agent -> nms SNMP2 TRAP COMMUNITY "public" OID "1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3"
}

FLOW snmp_v3_trap(agent, nms) {
    agent -> nms SNMP3 TRAP USER "admin" OID "1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3"
}

COMPILE {
        tcp_handshake(example_server, example_nms)
        snmp_v1_trap(example_server, example_nms)
        snmp_v2_trap(example_server, example_nms)
        snmp_v3_trap(example_server, example_nms)
}
```

## Examples Corpus (All 385 Verified Scenarios)
The following 385 verified `.fasm` scripts provide exhaustive examples and realistic traffic generation templates across all 81 protocols, frame modifiers, dual-stack pairs, and topologies.
### `examples/l2/arp/arp_explicit_hardware_override.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: ARP request and reply with explicit hardware and protocol address overrides.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, ARP, SHA, SPA, THA, TPA, REPLY, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define client endpoint.
HOST client_a {
    IP 172.16.0.10
    MAC 00:50:56:01:02:03
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define server endpoint.
HOST server_b {
    IP 172.16.0.20
    MAC 00:50:56:04:05:06
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define ARP flow with explicit SHA, SPA, THA, and TPA overrides.
FLOW arp_custom_hardware(src, dst) {
    src -> dst ARP SHA 00:50:56:01:02:03 SPA 172.16.0.10 THA 00:00:00:00:00:00 TPA 172.16.0.20
    src <- dst ARP REPLY SHA 00:50:56:04:05:06 SPA 172.16.0.20 THA 00:50:56:01:02:03 TPA 172.16.0.10
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing custom ARP hardware address exchange.
COMPILE {
    arp_custom_hardware(client_a, server_b)
}
```

// INSTRUCTION: Define BFD session node A.
HOST bfd_node_a { IP 10.200.1.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define BFD session node B.
HOST bfd_node_b { IP 10.200.1.2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define BFD control packet monitoring flow in State 3 (Up).
FLOW bfd_session_flow(a, b) {
    a -> b BFD STATE 3 MY_DISC 100 YOUR_DISC 200
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing BFD session packet.
COMPILE {
    bfd_session_flow(bfd_node_a, bfd_node_b)
}
```

```fasm
// PROMPT: BFD high-frequency session monitoring configuring minimum TX/RX intervals and detection multiplier.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, ->, <-, BFD, STATE, MY_DISC, YOUR_DISC, MIN_TX, MIN_RX, MULT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define leaf switch fast BFD peer.
HOST bfd_leaf { IP 10.0.100.2 }

FLOW bfd_fast_flow(s, l) {
    s -> l BFD STATE 3 MY_DISC 5001 YOUR_DISC 5002 MIN_TX 50000 MIN_RX 50000 MULT 3
    s <- l BFD STATE 3 MY_DISC 5002 YOUR_DISC 5001 MIN_TX 50000 MIN_RX 50000 MULT 3
}

### `examples/l3/bgp/bgp4_ipv6_peering.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Border Gateway Protocol 4+ peering over IPv6 using TCP 179 with OPEN and KEEPALIVE messages.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, ->, <-, BGP, OPEN, ASN, HOLDTIME, BGPID, KEEPALIVE, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define Autonomous System 65001 BGP router.
HOST bgp_peer_a { IP 2001:db8:ffff::1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define Autonomous System 65002 BGP router.
HOST bgp_peer_b { IP 2001:db8:ffff::2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define BGP-4+ session establishment and keepalive flow.
FLOW bgp_peer_flow(a, b) {
    a -> b BGP OPEN ASN 65001 HOLDTIME 180 BGPID 10.0.0.1
    a <- b BGP OPEN ASN 65002 HOLDTIME 180 BGPID 10.0.0.2
    a -> b BGP KEEPALIVE
    a <- b BGP KEEPALIVE
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing BGP IPv6 session.
COMPILE {
    bgp_peer_flow(bgp_peer_a, bgp_peer_b)
}
```
### `examples/l3/bgp/bgp_peer_open_and_keepalive.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: BGP peer session establishment and keepalive exchange on TCP port 179.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, ->, <-, BGP, OPEN, ASN, HOLDTIME, BGPID, KEEPALIVE, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define BGP edge router in Autonomous System 64512.
HOST bgp_speaker_1 { IP 192.0.2.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define BGP edge router in Autonomous System 64513.
HOST bgp_speaker_2 { IP 192.0.2.2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define BGP peering handshake flow exchanging OPEN parameters and KEEPALIVE markers.
FLOW bgp_peering_flow(peer1, peer2) {
    peer1 -> peer2 BGP OPEN ASN 64512 HOLDTIME 90 BGPID 192.0.2.1
    peer1 <- peer2 BGP OPEN ASN 64513 HOLDTIME 90 BGPID 192.0.2.2
    peer1 -> peer2 BGP KEEPALIVE
    peer1 <- peer2 BGP KEEPALIVE
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing BGP session establishment.
COMPILE {
    bgp_peering_flow(bgp_speaker_1, bgp_speaker_2)
}
```

    a -> b SCTP CHUNK INIT VTAG 0
    a <- b SCTP CHUNK INIT_ACK VTAG 100

### `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_3_way_handshake.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Establish a standard TCP 3-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) on HTTPS port 443 with explicit sequence and acknowledgment numbers.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, SEQ, ACKNUM, DSTPORT, SRCPORT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define an enterprise client with IP 10.10.10.10.
HOST enterprise_client { IP 10.10.10.10 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define an enterprise server with IP 10.20.20.20.
HOST enterprise_server { IP 10.20.20.20 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow representing a standard TCP 3-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK).
FLOW three_way_handshake(client, server) {
    client -> server TCP SYN SEQ 100 DSTPORT 443
    client <- server TCP SYN ACK SEQ 500 ACKNUM 101 SRCPORT 443
    client -> server TCP ACK SEQ 101 ACKNUM 501 DSTPORT 443
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the TCP handshake flow.
COMPILE {
    three_way_handshake(enterprise_client, enterprise_server)
}

```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate a TCP ACK firewall rule mapping probe to distinguish stateful vs unfiltered ports via unsolicited ACK packets and RST responses.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, ACK, RST, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, SEQ, ACKNUM, WIN, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow sending unsolicited TCP ACK segments to map firewall filtering rules on ports 22, 80, and 443.
FLOW ack_firewall_probe(auditor, firewall) {
    auditor -> firewall TCP ACK SRCPORT 44100 DSTPORT 22 SEQ 7777 ACKNUM 1 WIN 4096 WAIT 10ms
    auditor -> firewall TCP ACK SRCPORT 44101 DSTPORT 80 SEQ 7778 ACKNUM 1 WIN 4096 WAIT 10ms
    auditor <- firewall TCP RST SRCPORT 80 DSTPORT 44101 SEQ 1 WIN 0 WAIT 5ms
    auditor -> firewall TCP ACK SRCPORT 44102 DSTPORT 443 SEQ 7779 ACKNUM 1 WIN 4096 WAIT 10ms
    auditor <- firewall TCP RST SRCPORT 443 DSTPORT 44102 SEQ 1 WIN 0 WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the firewall ACK rule probe.

    ack_firewall_probe(auditor_box, perimeter_fw)
}

```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate a BGP-4 eBGP peering session establishment (OPEN, KEEP-ALIVE, UPDATE) between two autonomous system border routers on TCP port 179.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, PSH, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, SEQ, ACKNUM, WIN, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, s, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define AS65001 border router with IP 192.0.2.1 and MAC 00:00:5e:00:53:01.
HOST as65001_router { IP 192.0.2.1 MAC 00:00:5e:00:53:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define AS65002 border router with IP 192.0.2.2 and MAC 00:00:5e:00:53:02.
HOST as65002_router { IP 192.0.2.2 MAC 00:00:5e:00:53:02 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow establishing TCP port 179 connectivity and exchanging BGP OPEN, KEEPALIVE, and NLRI UPDATE messages.
FLOW bgp_peering_session(peer_a, peer_b) {
    peer_a -> peer_b TCP SYN SRCPORT 49179 DSTPORT 179 SEQ 10000 WIN 16384 WAIT 5ms
    peer_a <- peer_b TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 179 DSTPORT 49179 SEQ 20000 ACKNUM 10001 WIN 16384 WAIT 5ms
    peer_a -> peer_b TCP ACK SRCPORT 49179 DSTPORT 179 SEQ 10001 ACKNUM 20001 WIN 16384 WAIT 5ms
    peer_a -> peer_b TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 49179 DSTPORT 179 PAYLOAD "BGP4_OPEN_AS65001_HOLD180" WAIT 10ms
    peer_a <- peer_b TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 179 DSTPORT 49179 PAYLOAD "BGP4_OPEN_AS65002_HOLD180" WAIT 10ms
    peer_a -> peer_b TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 49179 DSTPORT 179 PAYLOAD "BGP4_KEEPALIVE" WAIT 1s
    peer_a <- peer_b TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 179 DSTPORT 49179 PAYLOAD "BGP4_KEEPALIVE" WAIT 1s
    peer_a -> peer_b TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 49179 DSTPORT 179 PAYLOAD "BGP4_UPDATE_NLRI_10.0.0.0/8" WAIT 50ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to run the BGP peering session flow.
COMPILE {
    bgp_peering_session(as65001_router, as65002_router)
}

### `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_bidirectional_asymmetric_port_routing.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Demonstrate automatic vs explicit TCP sequence and acknowledgment tracking across bidirectional arrows (-> and <-) when payload sizes vary.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, PSH, FIN, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, WIN, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a client endpoint relying on auto-calculated TCP sequence numbers with IP 10.203.0.10.
HOST auto_seq_client { IP 10.203.0.10 MAC 00:1a:2b:cb:00:0a }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a server endpoint relying on auto-calculated TCP sequence numbers with IP 10.203.0.20.
HOST auto_seq_server { IP 10.203.0.20 MAC 00:1a:2b:cb:00:14 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow exchanging variable-length payloads without manual SEQ/ACKNUM so the backend state machine computes exact byte advancements.
FLOW auto_sequence_tracking(client, server) {
    client -> server TCP SYN SRCPORT 40100 DSTPORT 8080 WIN 64240 WAIT 5ms
    client <- server TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 8080 DSTPORT 40100 WIN 64240 WAIT 5ms
    client -> server TCP ACK SRCPORT 40100 DSTPORT 8080 WIN 64240 WAIT 2ms
    client -> server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 40100 DSTPORT 8080 PAYLOAD "PING_12345" WAIT 5ms
    client <- server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 8080 DSTPORT 40100 PAYLOAD "PONG_ABCDEFGHIJ" WAIT 5ms
    client -> server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 40100 DSTPORT 8080 PAYLOAD "FINAL_BLOCK" WAIT 5ms
    client <- server TCP FIN ACK SRCPORT 8080 DSTPORT 40100 WAIT 5ms
    client -> server TCP FIN ACK SRCPORT 40100 DSTPORT 8080 WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to run the automatic TCP sequence tracking flow.
COMPILE {
    auto_sequence_tracking(auto_seq_client, auto_seq_server)
}
```
### `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_ecn_congestion_negotiation.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) negotiation and congestion window reduction using TCP SYN, ECE, CWR, and ACK flags.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, ECE, CWR, PSH, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, WIN, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

HOST dc_receiver { IP 10.100.1.20 MAC 00:25:90:aa:bb:02 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow negotiating ECN capability (SYN+ECE+CWR, SYN+ACK+ECE) followed by an ECN-Echo and CWR response.
FLOW ecn_congestion_control(sender, receiver) {
    sender -> receiver TCP SYN ECE CWR SRCPORT 55000 DSTPORT 9000 WIN 65535 WAIT 1ms
    sender <- receiver TCP SYN ACK ECE SRCPORT 9000 DSTPORT 55000 WIN 65535 WAIT 1ms
    sender -> receiver TCP ACK SRCPORT 55000 DSTPORT 9000 WIN 65535 WAIT 1ms
    sender -> receiver TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 55000 DSTPORT 9000 PAYLOAD "RDMA_BULK_BLOCK_01" WAIT 2ms
    sender <- receiver TCP ACK ECE SRCPORT 9000 DSTPORT 55000 WIN 32768 WAIT 1ms
    sender -> receiver TCP PSH ACK CWR SRCPORT 55000 DSTPORT 9000 WIN 32768 PAYLOAD "RDMA_BULK_BLOCK_02_THROTTLED" WAIT 2ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the ECN congestion control flow.
COMPILE {
    ecn_congestion_control(dc_sender, dc_receiver)
}
```

// PROMPT: Simulate a stealth TCP FIN scan probing closed and open ports on a target host.

    scanner -> target TCP FIN SRCPORT 51113 DSTPORT 3306 SEQ 0 WIN 2048 WAIT 10ms

```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate an FTP control session on TCP port 21 authenticating a user and entering passive mode (PASV) for directory listing.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, PSH, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define an FTP client workstation with IP 192.168.20.45.

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow performing FTP USER/PASS login and PASV mode negotiation on port 21.
FLOW ftp_control_session(client, server) {
    client -> server TCP SYN SRCPORT 50210 DSTPORT 21 WAIT 5ms
    client <- server TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 21 DSTPORT 50210 WAIT 5ms
    client -> server TCP ACK SRCPORT 50210 DSTPORT 21 WAIT 2ms

    client -> server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 50210 DSTPORT 21 PAYLOAD "USER anonymous" WAIT 10ms
    client <- server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 21 DSTPORT 50210 PAYLOAD "331 Please specify the password." WAIT 10ms
    client -> server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 50210 DSTPORT 21 PAYLOAD "PASS guest@example.com" WAIT 10ms
    client <- server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 21 DSTPORT 50210 PAYLOAD "230 Login successful." WAIT 10ms
    client -> server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 50210 DSTPORT 21 PAYLOAD "PASV" WAIT 10ms
    client <- server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 21 DSTPORT 50210 PAYLOAD "227 Entering Passive Mode (192,168,20,21,195,80)." WAIT 10ms
}

### `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_graceful_fin_teardown.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate a complete 4-way TCP graceful connection teardown using FIN and ACK flags with explicit sequence and acknowledgment numbers.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, FIN, SEQ, ACKNUM, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, WIN, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a web client endpoint with IP 192.168.10.25 and MAC 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e.
HOST web_client { IP 192.168.10.25 MAC 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e }

// INSTRUCTION: Define an origin server endpoint with IP 192.168.10.80 and MAC 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:80.
HOST origin_server { IP 192.168.10.80 MAC 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:80 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow that performs a 3-way handshake followed by a 4-way FIN-ACK connection teardown on port 8080.
FLOW graceful_teardown(client, server) {
    client -> server TCP SYN SRCPORT 50100 DSTPORT 8080 SEQ 1000 WIN 64240 WAIT 5ms
    client <- server TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 8080 DSTPORT 50100 SEQ 2000 ACKNUM 1001 WIN 65535 WAIT 5ms
    client -> server TCP ACK SRCPORT 50100 DSTPORT 8080 SEQ 1001 ACKNUM 2001 WIN 64240 WAIT 10ms
    client -> server TCP FIN ACK SRCPORT 50100 DSTPORT 8080 SEQ 1001 ACKNUM 2001 WIN 64240 WAIT 5ms
    client <- server TCP ACK SRCPORT 8080 DSTPORT 50100 SEQ 2001 ACKNUM 1002 WIN 65535 WAIT 5ms
    client <- server TCP FIN ACK SRCPORT 8080 DSTPORT 50100 SEQ 2001 ACKNUM 1002 WIN 65535 WAIT 5ms
    client -> server TCP ACK SRCPORT 50100 DSTPORT 8080 SEQ 1002 ACKNUM 2002 WIN 64240 WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the graceful TCP teardown flow.
COMPILE {
    graceful_teardown(web_client, origin_server)
}
```

```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate a complete HTTP/1.1 POST JSON authentication transaction over TCP port 8080 from handshake to FIN closure.

### `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_keepalive_long_idle_session.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate a long-lived idle TCP database connection using WAIT intervals in milliseconds (ms), seconds (s), and minutes (m) for TCP keepalives.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, PSH, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, SEQ, ACKNUM, WIN, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, s, m, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a backend worker host with IP 10.30.1.15.
HOST worker_node { IP 10.30.1.15 MAC 00:22:44:66:88:aa }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a PostgreSQL database server with IP 10.30.1.54.
HOST postgres_db { IP 10.30.1.54 MAC 00:22:44:66:88:bb }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow that connects on port 5432, idles for 1 minute, sends a TCP keepalive ACK, and runs a query after 5 seconds.
FLOW tcp_keepalive_idle(worker, db) {
    worker -> db TCP SYN SRCPORT 52400 DSTPORT 5432 SEQ 100 WIN 64240 WAIT 10ms
    worker <- db TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 5432 DSTPORT 52400 SEQ 500 ACKNUM 101 WIN 64240 WAIT 10ms
    worker -> db TCP ACK SRCPORT 52400 DSTPORT 5432 SEQ 101 ACKNUM 501 WIN 64240 WAIT 1m
    worker -> db TCP ACK SRCPORT 52400 DSTPORT 5432 SEQ 100 ACKNUM 501 WIN 64240 WAIT 5ms
    worker <- db TCP ACK SRCPORT 5432 DSTPORT 52400 SEQ 501 ACKNUM 101 WIN 64240 WAIT 5s
    worker -> db TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 52400 DSTPORT 5432 SEQ 101 ACKNUM 501 PAYLOAD "SELECT 1;" WAIT 20ms
    worker <- db TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 5432 DSTPORT 52400 SEQ 501 ACKNUM 110 PAYLOAD "ROW 1" WAIT 20ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to run the long-lived TCP keepalive session.
COMPILE {
    tcp_keepalive_idle(worker_node, postgres_db)
}
```
### `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_mqtt_iot_telemetry_publish.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate an IoT sensor publishing telemetry topics to an MQTT broker over TCP port 1883 with QoS 1 PUBACK acknowledgments.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, PSH, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, WIN, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE, LOOP

// INSTRUCTION: Define an IoT environmental sensor with IP 192.168.40.101.
HOST iot_sensor { IP 192.168.40.101 MAC b8:27:eb:10:20:30 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define an MQTT message broker with IP 192.168.40.10.
HOST mqtt_broker { IP 192.168.40.10 MAC b8:27:eb:00:00:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow for the initial MQTT TCP handshake and CONNECT/CONNACK exchange on port 1883.
FLOW mqtt_connect(sensor, broker) {
    sensor -> broker TCP SYN SRCPORT 41883 DSTPORT 1883 WIN 8192 WAIT 10ms
    sensor <- broker TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 1883 DSTPORT 41883 WIN 32768 WAIT 10ms
    sensor -> broker TCP ACK SRCPORT 41883 DSTPORT 1883 WIN 8192 WAIT 5ms
    sensor -> broker TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 41883 DSTPORT 1883 PAYLOAD "MQTT_CONNECT_sensor_101" WAIT 10ms
    sensor <- broker TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 1883 DSTPORT 41883 PAYLOAD "MQTT_CONNACK_0" WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow for publishing QoS 1 sensor telemetry and receiving PUBACK.
FLOW mqtt_publish_telemetry(sensor, broker) {
    sensor -> broker TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 41883 DSTPORT 1883 PAYLOAD "MQTT_PUBLISH_factory/temp_23.4C" WAIT 50ms
    sensor <- broker TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 1883 DSTPORT 41883 PAYLOAD "MQTT_PUBACK_MSGID_1" WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to connect once and publish telemetry 10 times in a loop.
COMPILE {
    mqtt_connect(iot_sensor, mqtt_broker)
    LOOP 10 {
        mqtt_publish_telemetry(iot_sensor, mqtt_broker)
    }
}
```
### `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_options_mss_wscale_sack_ts.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: TCP SYN negotiation with comprehensive TCP options including MSS, WSCALE, SACK_PERM, TSVAL, and TSECR.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, MSS, WSCALE, SACK_PERM, TSVAL, TSECR, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define client endpoint advertising TCP options.
HOST client_opt { IP 10.1.1.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define server endpoint answering with TCP options.
HOST server_opt { IP 10.1.1.2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define TCP options negotiation flow.
FLOW tcp_opt_flow(c, s) {
    c -> s TCP SYN SRCPORT 50000 DSTPORT 443 MSS 1460 WSCALE 7 SACK_PERM TSVAL 1000 TSECR 0
    c <- s TCP SYN ACK MSS 1460 WSCALE 7 SACK_PERM TSVAL 2000 TSECR 1000
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing TCP options negotiation.
COMPILE {
    tcp_opt_flow(client_opt, server_opt)
}
```

### `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_redis_resp_cache_lookup.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate a low-latency Redis RESP cache SET and GET pipeline over TCP port 6379.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, PSH, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, WIN, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE, LOOP

// INSTRUCTION: Define a web backend worker with IP 10.8.0.12.
HOST backend_worker { IP 10.8.0.12 MAC 02:42:0a:08:00:0c }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a Redis in-memory cache node with IP 10.8.0.63.
HOST redis_cache { IP 10.8.0.63 MAC 02:42:0a:08:00:3f }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow that connects to Redis port 6379 and executes RESP SET and GET commands.
FLOW redis_cache_pipeline(app, cache) {
    app -> cache TCP SYN SRCPORT 56379 DSTPORT 6379 WIN 65535 WAIT 1ms
    app <- cache TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 6379 DSTPORT 56379 WIN 65535 WAIT 1ms
    app -> cache TCP ACK SRCPORT 56379 DSTPORT 6379 WIN 65535 WAIT 1ms
    app -> cache TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 56379 DSTPORT 6379 PAYLOAD "SET session:1001 active" WAIT 1ms
    app <- cache TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 6379 DSTPORT 56379 PAYLOAD "+OK" WAIT 1ms
    app -> cache TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 56379 DSTPORT 6379 PAYLOAD "GET session:1001" WAIT 1ms
    app <- cache TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 6379 DSTPORT 56379 PAYLOAD "$6 active" WAIT 1ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the Redis cache lookup flow 5 times.
COMPILE {
    LOOP 5 {
        redis_cache_pipeline(backend_worker, redis_cache)
    }
}
```
### `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_retransmission_and_duplicate_ack.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate TCP fast retransmission triggered by three duplicate ACKs when an intermediate segment is lost in transit.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, PSH, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, SEQ, ACKNUM, WIN, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a video streaming server with IP 172.20.0.10.
HOST media_server { IP 172.20.0.10 MAC 00:aa:00:20:00:10 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a subscriber client with IP 172.20.0.99.
HOST subscriber_client { IP 172.20.0.99 MAC 00:aa:00:20:00:99 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow showing out-of-order segment arrival, 3 duplicate ACKs for SEQ 1011, and fast retransmission of the missing segment.
FLOW fast_retransmit_flow(server, client) {
    client -> server TCP SYN SRCPORT 58000 DSTPORT 8000 SEQ 200 WIN 65535 WAIT 5ms
    client <- server TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 8000 DSTPORT 58000 SEQ 1000 ACKNUM 201 WIN 65535 WAIT 5ms
    client -> server TCP ACK SRCPORT 58000 DSTPORT 8000 SEQ 201 ACKNUM 1001 WIN 65535 WAIT 5ms
    client <- server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 8000 DSTPORT 58000 SEQ 1001 ACKNUM 201 PAYLOAD "SEG_000001" WAIT 5ms
    client -> server TCP ACK SRCPORT 58000 DSTPORT 8000 SEQ 201 ACKNUM 1011 WIN 65535 WAIT 2ms
    client <- server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 8000 DSTPORT 58000 SEQ 1021 ACKNUM 201 PAYLOAD "SEG_000003" WAIT 5ms
    client -> server TCP ACK SRCPORT 58000 DSTPORT 8000 SEQ 201 ACKNUM 1011 WIN 65535 WAIT 2ms
    client <- server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 8000 DSTPORT 58000 SEQ 1031 ACKNUM 201 PAYLOAD "SEG_000004" WAIT 5ms
    client -> server TCP ACK SRCPORT 58000 DSTPORT 8000 SEQ 201 ACKNUM 1011 WIN 65535 WAIT 2ms
    client <- server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 8000 DSTPORT 58000 SEQ 1041 ACKNUM 201 PAYLOAD "SEG_000005" WAIT 5ms
    client -> server TCP ACK SRCPORT 58000 DSTPORT 8000 SEQ 201 ACKNUM 1011 WIN 65535 WAIT 2ms
    client <- server TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 8000 DSTPORT 58000 SEQ 1011 ACKNUM 201 PAYLOAD "SEG_000002" WAIT 5ms
    client -> server TCP ACK SRCPORT 58000 DSTPORT 8000 SEQ 201 ACKNUM 1051 WIN 65535 WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the TCP fast retransmission simulation.
COMPILE {
    fast_retransmit_flow(media_server, subscriber_client)
}
```

```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate an RFC 793 TCP simultaneous open handshake where two peer hosts send SYN packets concurrently and complete the connection with SYN-ACKs.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, PSH, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, SEQ, ACKNUM, WIN, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define peer alpha with IP 10.40.0.1 and MAC 02:40:00:00:00:01.

// INSTRUCTION: Define peer beta with IP 10.40.0.2 and MAC 02:40:00:00:00:02.
HOST peer_beta { IP 10.40.0.2 MAC 02:40:00:00:00:02 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow for a 4-packet TCP simultaneous open exchange on port 17900.
FLOW simultaneous_open(alpha, beta) {
    alpha -> beta TCP SYN SRCPORT 17900 DSTPORT 17900 SEQ 3000 WIN 65535 WAIT 1ms
    alpha <- beta TCP SYN SRCPORT 17900 DSTPORT 17900 SEQ 7000 WIN 65535 WAIT 1ms
    alpha -> beta TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 17900 DSTPORT 17900 SEQ 3000 ACKNUM 7001 WIN 65535 WAIT 2ms
    alpha <- beta TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 17900 DSTPORT 17900 SEQ 7000 ACKNUM 3001 WIN 65535 WAIT 2ms
    alpha -> beta TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 17900 DSTPORT 17900 SEQ 3001 ACKNUM 7001 PAYLOAD "P2P_ESTABLISHED" WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the simultaneous open TCP flow.
COMPILE {
    simultaneous_open(peer_alpha, peer_beta)
}

### `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_smtp_email_submission.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate an SMTP email submission conversation over TCP port 587 including EHLO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA, and QUIT commands.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, PSH, FIN, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a mail user agent host with IP 10.15.0.25.
HOST mail_client { IP 10.15.0.25 MAC 00:11:32:aa:bb:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define an SMTP mail relay server with IP 10.15.0.10.
HOST smtp_relay { IP 10.15.0.10 MAC 00:11:32:aa:bb:02 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow simulating an SMTP mail submission dialog on port 587.
FLOW smtp_mail_submission(mua, mta) {
    mua -> mta TCP SYN SRCPORT 49800 DSTPORT 587 WAIT 5ms
    mua <- mta TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 587 DSTPORT 49800 WAIT 5ms
    mua -> mta TCP ACK SRCPORT 49800 DSTPORT 587 WAIT 2ms
    mua <- mta TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 587 DSTPORT 49800 PAYLOAD "220 smtp.example.com ESMTP" WAIT 10ms
    mua -> mta TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 49800 DSTPORT 587 PAYLOAD "EHLO client.example.com" WAIT 10ms
    mua <- mta TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 587 DSTPORT 49800 PAYLOAD "250-smtp.example.com" WAIT 10ms
    mua -> mta TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 49800 DSTPORT 587 PAYLOAD "MAIL FROM:<alice@example.com>" WAIT 10ms
    mua <- mta TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 587 DSTPORT 49800 PAYLOAD "250 2.1.0 Ok" WAIT 10ms
    mua -> mta TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 49800 DSTPORT 587 PAYLOAD "RCPT TO:<bob@example.com>" WAIT 10ms
    mua <- mta TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 587 DSTPORT 49800 PAYLOAD "250 2.1.5 Ok" WAIT 10ms
    mua -> mta TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 49800 DSTPORT 587 PAYLOAD "QUIT" WAIT 5ms
    mua <- mta TCP FIN ACK SRCPORT 587 DSTPORT 49800 PAYLOAD "221 2.0.0 Bye" WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the SMTP email submission flow.
COMPILE {
    smtp_mail_submission(mail_client, smtp_relay)
}
```
### `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_syn_ack_reflection_amplification.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate a TCP SYN-ACK reflection attack where a reflector server sends unsolicited SYN-ACK packets to a spoofed victim IP in a loop.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, RST, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, SEQ, ACKNUM, WIN, WAIT, ms, COMPILE, LOOP

// INSTRUCTION: Define the spoofed victim host with IP 192.0.2.50.
HOST spoofed_victim { IP 192.0.2.50 MAC 00:50:56:c0:00:08 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a public reflector server with IP 198.51.100.200.
HOST reflector_server { IP 198.51.100.200 MAC 00:50:56:c0:00:09 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow where the victim receives reflected SYN-ACK packets from port 80 and replies with RST.
FLOW syn_ack_reflection(victim, reflector) {
    victim <- reflector TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 80 DSTPORT 53000 SEQ 40000 ACKNUM 1001 WIN 65535 WAIT 2ms
    victim -> reflector TCP RST SRCPORT 53000 DSTPORT 80 SEQ 1001 WIN 0 WAIT 2ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to repeat the SYN-ACK reflection 20 times.
COMPILE {
    LOOP 20 {
        syn_ack_reflection(spoofed_victim, reflector_server)
    }
}

### `examples/l4/tcp/tcp_zero_window_probe_and_recovery.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate TCP receiver buffer exhaustion advertising a zero window (WIN 0), a zero-window probe, and subsequent window recovery (WIN 65535).
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, TCP, SYN, ACK, PSH, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, SEQ, ACKNUM, WIN, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, s, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a bulk storage sender with IP 10.20.0.10.
HOST storage_sender { IP 10.20.0.10 MAC 00:1b:21:aa:00:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a slow ingestion receiver with IP 10.20.0.20.
HOST slow_receiver { IP 10.20.0.20 MAC 00:1b:21:aa:00:02 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow showing window shrinkage to 0, a 1-byte zero-window probe after 1s, and a window update back to 65535.
FLOW zero_window_recovery(sender, receiver) {
    sender -> receiver TCP SYN SRCPORT 42000 DSTPORT 9100 SEQ 1000 WIN 64240 WAIT 5ms
    sender <- receiver TCP SYN ACK SRCPORT 9100 DSTPORT 42000 SEQ 5000 ACKNUM 1001 WIN 4096 WAIT 5ms
    sender -> receiver TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 42000 DSTPORT 9100 SEQ 1001 ACKNUM 5001 WIN 64240 PAYLOAD "CHUNK_FILLING_BUFFER" WAIT 10ms
    sender <- receiver TCP ACK SRCPORT 9100 DSTPORT 42000 SEQ 5001 ACKNUM 1021 WIN 0 WAIT 1s
    sender -> receiver TCP ACK SRCPORT 42000 DSTPORT 9100 SEQ 1020 ACKNUM 5001 WIN 64240 PAYLOAD "Z" WAIT 10ms
    sender <- receiver TCP ACK SRCPORT 9100 DSTPORT 42000 SEQ 5001 ACKNUM 1021 WIN 0 WAIT 500ms
    sender <- receiver TCP ACK SRCPORT 9100 DSTPORT 42000 SEQ 5001 ACKNUM 1021 WIN 65535 WAIT 5ms
    sender -> receiver TCP PSH ACK SRCPORT 42000 DSTPORT 9100 SEQ 1021 ACKNUM 5001 WIN 64240 PAYLOAD "RESUMED_STREAM_DATA" WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the TCP zero-window probe and recovery scenario.
COMPILE {
    zero_window_recovery(storage_sender, slow_receiver)
}
```

// PROMPT: Simulate a complete DHCPv4 DORA (Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge) lease allocation exchange over UDP ports 67 and 68 using broadcast and server endpoints.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define an unconfigured DHCP client with IP 0.0.0.0 and client MAC 00:0a:95:9d:68:16.
HOST dhcp_client { IP 0.0.0.0 MAC 00:0a:95:9d:68:16 }

HOST dhcp_server { IP 192.168.1.1 MAC 00:0a:95:00:00:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a 3-argument flow modeling DHCPDISCOVER, DHCPOFFER, DHCPREQUEST, and DHCPACK on UDP ports 68 and 67.
FLOW dhcp_dora_handshake(client, bcast, server) {

// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a workstation querying for local printers with IP 192.168.1.30.
HOST mdns_querier { IP 192.168.1.30 MAC ac:de:48:00:11:22 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a network printer advertising _ipp._tcp.local with IP 192.168.1.210.
HOST network_printer { IP 192.168.1.210 MAC ac:de:48:00:33:44 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define the mDNS IPv4 multicast address 224.0.0.251 with multicast MAC 01:00:5e:00:00:fb.
HOST mdns_group { IP 224.0.0.251 MAC 01:00:5e:00:00:fb }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow where the querier and printer exchange mDNS PTR/SRV records via the multicast group on port 5353.
FLOW mdns_printer_lookup(querier, printer, group) {
    querier -> group UDP SRCPORT 5353 DSTPORT 5353 PAYLOAD "MDNS_QUERY_PTR_ipp_tcp_local" WAIT 15ms
    printer -> group UDP SRCPORT 5353 DSTPORT 5353 PAYLOAD "MDNS_ANSWER_SRV_office_printer_local_631" WAIT 15ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the mDNS local service lookup.
COMPILE {
    mdns_printer_lookup(mdns_querier, network_printer, mdns_group)
}
```

### `examples/l4/udp/udp_ntp_clock_synchronization.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate Network Time Protocol (NTP) clock synchronization polling between a Linux host and a Stratum-1 NTP server on UDP port 123 with 1s wait intervals.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, s, COMPILE, LOOP

// INSTRUCTION: Define an internal application server requiring clock sync with IP 10.10.5.20.
HOST ntp_client { IP 10.10.5.20 MAC 00:15:5d:01:05:14 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a GPS-backed Stratum-1 NTP server with IP 10.10.5.1.
HOST stratum1_ntp { IP 10.10.5.1 MAC 00:15:5d:01:05:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow that sends an NTPv4 client request on UDP port 123 and receives a server timestamp reply.
FLOW ntp_time_sync(client, server) {
    client -> server UDP SRCPORT 123 DSTPORT 123 PAYLOAD "NTPv4_MODE3_CLIENT_REQ" WAIT 1s
    client <- server UDP SRCPORT 123 DSTPORT 123 PAYLOAD "NTPv4_MODE4_STRATUM1_GPS" WAIT 1s
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to run 4 NTP polling cycles.
COMPILE {
    LOOP 4 {
        ntp_time_sync(ntp_client, stratum1_ntp)
    }
}
```
### `examples/l4/udp/udp_quic_http3_initial_exchange.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate an HTTP/3 over QUIC initial connection establishment and 0-RTT stream exchange on UDP port 443.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a browser client supporting HTTP/3 with IP 192.168.1.77.
HOST h3_browser { IP 192.168.1.77 MAC f0:18:98:aa:bb:cc }

// INSTRUCTION: Define an edge CDN server listening on UDP 443 with IP 198.51.100.88.
HOST cdn_edge { IP 198.51.100.88 MAC f0:18:98:dd:ee:ff }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow sending QUIC Initial, Handshake, and 1-RTT HTTP/3 GET frames over UDP port 443.
FLOW quic_http3_exchange(browser, cdn) {
    browser -> cdn UDP SRCPORT 55443 DSTPORT 443 PAYLOAD "QUIC_INITIAL_TLS13_CLIENT_HELLO" WAIT 5ms
    browser <- cdn UDP SRCPORT 443 DSTPORT 55443 PAYLOAD "QUIC_INITIAL_SERVER_HELLO_HANDSHAKE" WAIT 5ms
    browser -> cdn UDP SRCPORT 55443 DSTPORT 443 PAYLOAD "QUIC_1RTT_H3_HEADERS_GET_INDEX" WAIT 5ms
    browser <- cdn UDP SRCPORT 443 DSTPORT 55443 PAYLOAD "QUIC_1RTT_H3_DATA_200_OK" WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to run the QUIC HTTP/3 connection flow.
COMPILE {
    quic_http3_exchange(h3_browser, cdn_edge)
}
```
### `examples/l4/udp/udp_radius_authentication_accounting.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate 802.1X RADIUS authentication on UDP port 1812 and RADIUS accounting start/response on UDP port 1813 between a wireless controller and AAA server.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a wireless LAN controller (NAS) with IP 10.5.10.2.

// INSTRUCTION: Define a FreeRADIUS AAA server with IP 10.5.10.100.
HOST radius_aaa_server { IP 10.5.10.100 MAC 00:24:97:10:20:64 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow performing RADIUS Access-Request/Access-Accept on port 1812 and Accounting-Request/Accounting-Response on port 1813.
FLOW radius_auth_and_acct(nas, aaa) {
    nas -> aaa UDP SRCPORT 41812 DSTPORT 1812 PAYLOAD "RADIUS_ACCESS_REQUEST_user=jdoe" WAIT 10ms
    nas <- aaa UDP SRCPORT 1812 DSTPORT 41812 PAYLOAD "RADIUS_ACCESS_ACCEPT_vlan=20" WAIT 10ms
    nas -> aaa UDP SRCPORT 41813 DSTPORT 1813 PAYLOAD "RADIUS_ACCT_START_sess=9981" WAIT 10ms
    nas <- aaa UDP SRCPORT 1813 DSTPORT 41813 PAYLOAD "RADIUS_ACCT_RESPONSE_ok" WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the RADIUS authentication and accounting flow.
COMPILE {
    radius_auth_and_acct(wlan_controller, radius_aaa_server)
}

### `examples/l4/udp/udp_rtp_voice_media_stream.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate a bidirectional G.711 RTP voice media stream exchanging 20ms audio frames on UDP port 16384 in a loop.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE, LOOP

// INSTRUCTION: Define VoIP endpoint A with IP 10.60.2.11.
HOST rtp_endpoint_a { IP 10.60.2.11 MAC 00:04:f2:aa:00:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define VoIP endpoint B with IP 10.60.2.12.
HOST rtp_endpoint_b { IP 10.60.2.12 MAC 00:04:f2:aa:00:02 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow exchanging bidirectional RTP G.711 PCMU audio payloads with 20ms pacing.
FLOW rtp_audio_frame(ep_a, ep_b) {
    ep_a -> ep_b UDP SRCPORT 16384 DSTPORT 16384 PAYLOAD "RTP_PT0_PCMU_160B_A2B" WAIT 20ms
    ep_a <- ep_b UDP SRCPORT 16384 DSTPORT 16384 PAYLOAD "RTP_PT0_PCMU_160B_B2A" WAIT 20ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to stream 25 bidirectional RTP frames.
COMPILE {
    LOOP 25 {
        rtp_audio_frame(rtp_endpoint_a, rtp_endpoint_b)
    }
}

### `examples/l4/udp/udp_sip_voip_call_setup.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate a VoIP SIP call setup and teardown signaling sequence (INVITE, 100 Trying, 180 Ringing, 200 OK, ACK, BYE) over UDP port 5060.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, s, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define Caller IP Phone A with IP 10.60.1.101.
HOST sip_phone_a { IP 10.60.1.101 MAC 00:04:f2:11:11:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define IP PBX SIP Proxy with IP 10.60.1.10.
HOST sip_pbx_proxy { IP 10.60.1.10 MAC 00:04:f2:00:00:10 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow modeling SIP call signaling over UDP port 5060.
FLOW sip_call_signaling(phone, pbx) {
    phone -> pbx UDP SRCPORT 5060 DSTPORT 5060 PAYLOAD "INVITE sip:2002@pbx.local SIP/2.0" WAIT 10ms
    phone <- pbx UDP SRCPORT 5060 DSTPORT 5060 PAYLOAD "SIP/2.0 100 Trying" WAIT 20ms
    phone <- pbx UDP SRCPORT 5060 DSTPORT 5060 PAYLOAD "SIP/2.0 180 Ringing" WAIT 1s
    phone <- pbx UDP SRCPORT 5060 DSTPORT 5060 PAYLOAD "SIP/2.0 200 OK SDP_G711U" WAIT 10ms
    phone -> pbx UDP SRCPORT 5060 DSTPORT 5060 PAYLOAD "ACK sip:2002@pbx.local SIP/2.0" WAIT 2s
    phone -> pbx UDP SRCPORT 5060 DSTPORT 5060 PAYLOAD "BYE sip:2002@pbx.local SIP/2.0" WAIT 10ms
    phone <- pbx UDP SRCPORT 5060 DSTPORT 5060 PAYLOAD "SIP/2.0 200 OK" WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the SIP VoIP signaling flow.
COMPILE {
    sip_call_signaling(sip_phone_a, sip_pbx_proxy)
}
```
### `examples/l4/udp/udp_ssdp_upnp_multicast_discovery.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate UPnP Simple Service Discovery Protocol (SSDP) M-SEARCH multicast discovery on UDP port 1900 and unicast device response.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a smart home controller host with IP 192.168.1.20.
HOST smart_controller { IP 192.168.1.20 MAC dc:a6:32:00:01:20 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define the SSDP IPv4 multicast group endpoint 239.255.255.250 with Ethernet multicast MAC 01:00:5e:7f:ff:fa.
HOST ssdp_multicast { IP 239.255.255.250 MAC 01:00:5e:7f:ff:fa }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a UPnP smart TV responder with IP 192.168.1.85.
HOST smart_tv_device { IP 192.168.1.85 MAC dc:a6:32:00:01:85 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a 3-host flow sending an SSDP multicast M-SEARCH and receiving a unicast HTTP/1.1 200 OK UDP response.
FLOW ssdp_discovery(controller, mcast, device) {
    controller -> mcast UDP SRCPORT 51900 DSTPORT 1900 PAYLOAD "M-SEARCH * HTTP/1.1 ST:ssdp:all" WAIT 10ms
    controller <- device UDP SRCPORT 1900 DSTPORT 51900 PAYLOAD "HTTP/1.1 200 OK LOCATION:http://192.168.1.85/desc.xml" WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to run the SSDP discovery flow.
COMPILE {
    ssdp_discovery(smart_controller, ssdp_multicast, smart_tv_device)
}
```
### `examples/l4/udp/udp_stateless_empty_payload_ping.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Send minimal zero-length UDP datagrams without PAYLOAD using both default ports and explicit high-numbered ports for traceroute probing.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, ->, <-, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a traceroute source host with IP 10.0.1.10.
HOST trace_source { IP 10.0.1.10 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a traceroute destination host with IP 10.0.9.99.
HOST trace_dest { IP 10.0.9.99 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow sending empty UDP probe packets to high ports 33434, 33435, and default port.
FLOW empty_udp_probes(src, dst) {
    src -> dst UDP WAIT 5ms
    src -> dst UDP SRCPORT 45000 DSTPORT 33434 WAIT 5ms
    src -> dst UDP SRCPORT 45001 DSTPORT 33435 WAIT 5ms
    src <- dst UDP SRCPORT 33435 DSTPORT 45001 WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the minimal UDP probe flow.
COMPILE {
    empty_udp_probes(trace_source, trace_dest)
}
```

```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate RFC 5424 Syslog security audit messages forwarded over UDP port 514 from an edge router to a SIEM log collector.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

    router -> collector UDP SRCPORT 51514 DSTPORT 514 PAYLOAD "<27>1 2026-10-21T12:00:03Z router01 kernel - -LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface Gi0/1" WAIT 15ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to emit the syslog event batch.

    forward_syslog_events(edge_router, siem_collector)
}

### `examples/l4/udp/udp_tftp_firmware_block_transfer.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate a PXE network boot TFTP firmware read request (RRQ) on UDP port 69 followed by numbered data blocks and acknowledgments on ephemeral ports.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, UDP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, PAYLOAD, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a diskless PXE boot client with IP 192.168.100.55.
HOST pxe_client { IP 192.168.100.55 MAC 52:54:00:12:34:55 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a TFTP provisioning server with IP 192.168.100.10.
HOST tftp_server { IP 192.168.100.10 MAC 52:54:00:12:34:10 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow that requests boot.bin on UDP port 69 and transfers two 512-byte TFTP data blocks with ACKs.
FLOW tftp_firmware_transfer(client, server) {
    client -> server UDP SRCPORT 50069 DSTPORT 69 PAYLOAD "TFTP_RRQ_boot.bin_octet" WAIT 5ms
    client <- server UDP SRCPORT 61000 DSTPORT 50069 PAYLOAD "TFTP_DATA_BLK1_512B" WAIT 5ms
    client -> server UDP SRCPORT 50069 DSTPORT 61000 PAYLOAD "TFTP_ACK_BLK1" WAIT 2ms
    client <- server UDP SRCPORT 61000 DSTPORT 50069 PAYLOAD "TFTP_DATA_BLK2_EOF" WAIT 5ms
    client -> server UDP SRCPORT 50069 DSTPORT 61000 PAYLOAD "TFTP_ACK_BLK2" WAIT 2ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to run the TFTP firmware download simulation.
COMPILE {
    tftp_firmware_transfer(pxe_client, tftp_server)
}
```

// PROMPT: Simulate a WireGuard VPN Noise_IKpsk2 handshake initiation, response, and encrypted transport data exchange over UDP port 51820.

### `examples/l7/dhcp/dhcp_dual_stack_v4_v6.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Dual-stack dynamic host configuration with DHCPv4 Discover (68->67) and DHCPv6 Solicit (546->547).
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, ->, DHCP, DISCOVER, SOLICIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define unconfigured IPv4 client.
HOST dhcp_v4_client { IP 0.0.0.0 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define IPv4 broadcast DHCP server.
HOST dhcp_v4_server { IP 255.255.255.255 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define link-local IPv6 client.
HOST dhcp_v6_client { IP fe80::10 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define all-DHCP-relay-and-servers IPv6 multicast group.
HOST dhcp_v6_server { IP ff02::1:2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define dual-stack DHCP configuration flow.
FLOW dhcp_dual_flow(c4, s4, c6, s6) {
    c4 -> s4 DHCP DISCOVER
    c6 -> s6 DHCP SOLICIT
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing dual-stack host discovery.
COMPILE {
    dhcp_dual_flow(dhcp_v4_client, dhcp_v4_server, dhcp_v6_client, dhcp_v6_server)
}
```

// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, ->, KERBEROS, AS_REQ, REALM, LDAP, BIND_REQ, MSGID, BASE_DN, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define enterprise directory client.
HOST directory_client { IP 10.10.1.50 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define enterprise domain controller.
HOST domain_controller { IP 10.10.1.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define directory authentication and search flow.
FLOW auth_directory_flow(c, dc) {
    c -> dc KERBEROS AS_REQ REALM "CORP.LOCAL"
    c -> dc LDAP BIND_REQ MSGID 1 BASE_DN "dc=corp,dc=local"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing Kerberos and LDAP transactions.
COMPILE {
    auth_directory_flow(directory_client, domain_controller)
}
```

    w -> s SMB COMMAND SESSION_SETUP

### `examples/l7/smtp/smtp_mail_transaction_rfc5321.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Complete RFC 5321 SMTP email delivery transaction from sender to recipient.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, ->, <-, SMTP, MAIL_FROM, RCPT_TO, PARAM, CODE, REPLY, BODY, QUIT, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define client endpoint.
HOST client { IP 10.0.0.5 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define server endpoint.
HOST server { IP 10.0.0.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define application traffic flow.
FLOW smtp_txn(c, s) {
    c -> s SMTP MAIL_FROM PARAM "alice@corp.net"
    c <- s SMTP CODE 250 REPLY "250 Sender OK"
    c -> s SMTP RCPT_TO PARAM "bob@corp.net"
    c <- s SMTP CODE 250 REPLY "250 Recipient OK"
    c -> s SMTP BODY "Subject: Test Alert\r\n\r\nSystem check completed successfully."
    c <- s SMTP CODE 250 REPLY "250 Queued mail for delivery"
    c -> s SMTP QUIT
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing the flow scenario.
COMPILE {
    smtp_txn(client, server)
}
```
### `examples/l7/snmp/snmpv1/snmpv1_all_supported_v1_varbind_types.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Generate an SNMPv1 trap containing all 7 SMIv1-compatible VARBIND types (STRING, INT, TIMETICKS, IPVAL, OIDVAL, COUNTER32, GAUGE32) in a single packet.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, SNMP1, TRAP, COMMUNITY, ENTERPRISE, AGENTIP, GENTRAP, SPECTRAP, SYSUPTIME, VARBIND, STRING, INT, TIMETICKS, IPVAL, OIDVAL, COUNTER32, GAUGE32, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a multi-service edge router with IP 10.108.0.1.
HOST edge_agent { IP 10.108.0.1 MAC 00:1a:a1:08:00:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define an SMIv1 trap receiver with IP 10.108.0.100.
HOST smiv1_nms { IP 10.108.0.100 MAC 00:1a:a1:08:00:64 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow sending a single SNMPv1 trap carrying STRING, INT, TIMETICKS, IPVAL, OIDVAL, COUNTER32, and GAUGE32 varbinds.
FLOW snmpv1_all_smiv1_varbinds(agent, nms) {
    agent -> nms SNMP1 TRAP COMMUNITY "public" ENTERPRISE 1.3.6.1.4.1.8072 AGENTIP 10.108.0.1 GENTRAP 6 SPECTRAP 99 SYSUPTIME 50000 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "edge-rtr-01" VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.1.0 INT 24 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0 TIMETICKS 50000 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.4.20.1.1.10.108.0.1 IPVAL 10.108.0.1 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0 OIDVAL 1.3.6.1.4.1.8072.3.2.10 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.10.1 COUNTER32 9876543 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5.1 GAUGE32 1000000000
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to emit the multi-varbind SNMPv1 trap.
COMPILE {
    snmpv1_all_smiv1_varbinds(edge_agent, smiv1_nms)
}
```

### `examples/l7/snmp/snmpv1/snmpv1_custom_ports_and_community.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Send SNMPv1 traps to a non-standard high UDP port (10162) with a custom SRCPORT, custom COMMUNITY string, and 500ms WAIT delay.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, SNMP1, TRAP, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, COMMUNITY, OID, ENTERPRISE, GENTRAP, SPECTRAP, SYSUPTIME, VARBIND, INT, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define an unprivileged container SNMP agent with IP 10.200.1.50.
HOST container_agent { IP 10.200.1.50 MAC 02:42:0a:c8:01:32 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a non-root trap daemon host listening on UDP port 10162 with IP 10.200.1.10.
HOST custom_trapd { IP 10.200.1.10 MAC 02:42:0a:c8:01:0a }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow sending SNMPv1 traps from SRCPORT 55161 to DSTPORT 10162 with a 500ms interval.
FLOW custom_port_snmpv1(agent, trapd) {
    agent -> trapd SNMP1 TRAP SRCPORT 55161 DSTPORT 10162 COMMUNITY "custom_sec_v1" OID "1.3.6.1.4.1.8072.2.3.0.1" ENTERPRISE 1.3.6.1.4.1.8072.2.3 GENTRAP 6 SPECTRAP 1 SYSUPTIME 6000 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.4.1.8072.2.1.1.0 INT 100 WAIT 500ms
    agent -> trapd SNMP1 TRAP SRCPORT 55161 DSTPORT 10162 COMMUNITY "custom_sec_v1" OID "1.3.6.1.4.1.8072.2.3.0.2" ENTERPRISE 1.3.6.1.4.1.8072.2.3 GENTRAP 6 SPECTRAP 2 SYSUPTIME 6050 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.4.1.8072.2.1.1.0 INT 200 WAIT 500ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to run the custom-port SNMPv1 trap flow.
COMPILE {
    custom_port_snmpv1(container_agent, custom_trapd)
}
```

### `examples/l7/snmp/snmpv1/snmpv1_multi_switch_trap_aggregation.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate three access-layer switches concurrently reporting SNMPv1 linkStatus and spanning-tree topology traps to a central NMS.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, SNMP1, TRAP, COMMUNITY, ENTERPRISE, AGENTIP, GENTRAP, SPECTRAP, SYSUPTIME, VARBIND, INT, STRING, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define access switch 1 with IP 10.110.0.11.
HOST access_sw1 { IP 10.110.0.11 MAC 00:1b:0d:11:00:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define access switch 2 with IP 10.110.0.12.
HOST access_sw2 { IP 10.110.0.12 MAC 00:1b:0d:11:00:02 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define access switch 3 with IP 10.110.0.13.
HOST access_sw3 { IP 10.110.0.13 MAC 00:1b:0d:11:00:03 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define the campus NMS server with IP 10.110.0.254.
HOST campus_nms { IP 10.110.0.254 MAC 00:1b:0d:11:00:fe }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a 4-parameter flow collecting SNMPv1 traps from all three access switches.
FLOW campus_switch_traps(sw1, sw2, sw3, nms) {
    sw1 -> nms SNMP1 TRAP COMMUNITY "campus_ro" ENTERPRISE 1.3.6.1.2.1.17 AGENTIP 10.110.0.11 GENTRAP 6 SPECTRAP 1 SYSUPTIME 10000 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "access-sw1-newRoot" WAIT 10ms
    sw2 -> nms SNMP1 TRAP COMMUNITY "campus_ro" ENTERPRISE 1.3.6.1.2.1.17 AGENTIP 10.110.0.12 GENTRAP 6 SPECTRAP 2 SYSUPTIME 10020 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "access-sw2-topologyChange" WAIT 10ms
    sw3 -> nms SNMP1 TRAP COMMUNITY "campus_ro" ENTERPRISE 1.3.6.1.2.1.17 AGENTIP 10.110.0.13 GENTRAP 2 SPECTRAP 0 SYSUPTIME 10040 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1.24 INT 24 WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the multi-switch SNMPv1 trap aggregation flow.
COMPILE {
    campus_switch_traps(access_sw1, access_sw2, access_sw3, campus_nms)
}
```
### `examples/l7/snmp/snmpv1/snmpv1_non_trap_pdus_rfc1157.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: RFC 1157 SNMPv1 non-trap PDUs including GET, GETNEXT, SET, and RESPONSE emitting BER tags.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, ->, <-, SNMP1, GET, GETNEXT, SET, RESPONSE, COMMUNITY, OID, VARBIND, STRING, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define SNMP management station.
HOST snmp1_client { IP 10.0.1.1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define SNMP managed agent.
HOST snmp1_agent { IP 10.0.1.2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define full SNMPv1 CRUD request and response flow.
FLOW snmp1_crud_flow(c, a) {
    c -> a SNMP1 GET COMMUNITY "public" OID "1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0"
    c -> a SNMP1 GETNEXT COMMUNITY "public" OID "1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0"
    c -> a SNMP1 SET COMMUNITY "private" VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "core-router"
    c <- a SNMP1 RESPONSE COMMUNITY "public" VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 STRING "Linux 6.0"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing SNMPv1 non-trap PDUs.
COMPILE {
    snmp1_crud_flow(snmp1_client, snmp1_agent)
}
```

```fasm
// PROMPT: Generate an SNMPv1 optical transceiver DOM alert trap carrying negative signed 32-bit integers (INT -18 and INT -24) representing RX/TX optical power in dBm.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, SNMP1, TRAP, COMMUNITY, ENTERPRISE, AGENTIP, GENTRAP, SPECTRAP, SYSUPTIME, VARBIND, INT, STRING, COMPILE

```fasm
// PROMPT: Generate an SNMPv1 warmStart generic trap (GENTRAP 1) demonstrating both automatic RFC 1157 OID mapping (1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.2) and explicit GENTRAP configuration.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, SNMP1, TRAP, COMMUNITY, OID, ENTERPRISE, AGENTIP, GENTRAP, SPECTRAP, SYSUPTIME, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

HOST dist_switch { IP 10.101.0.2 MAC 00:1c:73:00:01:02 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define an NMS server with IP 10.101.0.100.
HOST nms_collector { IP 10.101.0.100 MAC 00:1c:73:00:01:64 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow sending SNMPv1 warmStart traps via auto-mapped OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.2 and explicit GENTRAP 1.
FLOW snmpv1_warm_start(agent, nms) {

    agent -> nms SNMP1 TRAP COMMUNITY "public" ENTERPRISE 1.3.6.1.4.1.30065 AGENTIP 10.101.0.2 GENTRAP 1 SPECTRAP 0 SYSUPTIME 4505 WAIT 20ms

```fasm
// PROMPT: Demonstrate all 9 supported FrameAssembly VARBIND value types (NULLVAL, STRING, INT, TIMETICKS, IPVAL, OIDVAL, COUNTER32, GAUGE32, COUNTER64) within a single SNMPv2c RESPONSE packet.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, SNMP2, GET, RESPONSE, COMMUNITY, REQID, VARBIND, NULLVAL, STRING, INT, TIMETICKS, IPVAL, OIDVAL, COUNTER32, GAUGE32, COUNTER64, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a comprehensive MIB test client with IP 10.127.0.10.
HOST mib_tester { IP 10.127.0.10 MAC 00:16:3e:27:00:10 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a reference SNMPv2c agent with IP 10.127.0.20.
HOST ref_snmp_agent { IP 10.127.0.20 MAC 00:16:3e:27:00:20 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow that sends an SNMPv2c GET and receives a RESPONSE containing all 9 VarBind data types.
FLOW snmpv2c_all_nine_varbinds(tester, agent) {
    tester -> agent SNMP2 GET COMMUNITY "all_types" REQID 9999 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 NULLVAL WAIT 10ms
    tester <- agent SNMP2 RESPONSE COMMUNITY "all_types" REQID 9999 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.4.0 NULLVAL VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "ref-agent-01" VARBIND 1.3.6.1.4.1.9999.1.1.0 INT -42 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0 TIMETICKS 360000 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.4.20.1.1.10.127.0.20 IPVAL 10.127.0.20 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0 OIDVAL 1.3.6.1.4.1.8072.3.2.10 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.10.1 COUNTER32 500000 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5.1 GAUGE32 100000000 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.6.1 COUNTER64 9876543210123 WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the 9-varbind SNMPv2c showcase flow.
COMPILE {
    snmpv2c_all_nine_varbinds(mib_tester, ref_snmp_agent)
}
```

```fasm
// PROMPT: Demonstrate implicit default TRAP PDU encoding in SNMP1, SNMP2, and SNMP3 statements when the PDU type keyword is omitted.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, SNMP1, SNMP2, SNMP3, COMMUNITY, USER, OID, SYSUPTIME, VARBIND, STRING, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

HOST unified_trapd { IP 10.137.0.100 MAC 00:1a:2b:37:00:64 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow omitting the explicit TRAP keyword to verify default Trap PDU generation on port 162 across SNMP1, SNMP2, and SNMP3.
FLOW implicit_trap_pdu_flow(agent, trapd) {
    agent -> trapd SNMP1 COMMUNITY "public" OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.1 SYSUPTIME 1000 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "v1-default-trap" WAIT 10ms
    agent -> trapd SNMP2 COMMUNITY "public" OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3 SYSUPTIME 2000 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "v2c-default-trap" WAIT 10ms
    agent -> trapd SNMP3 USER "trap_user" OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.4 SYSUPTIME 3000 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "v3-default-trap" WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the implicit default trap PDU flow.

    implicit_trap_pdu_flow(default_pdu_agent, unified_trapd)
}

### `examples/l7/snmp/snmpv2c/snmpv2c_getnext_mib_walk.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate an snmpwalk MIB tree traversal using sequential SNMPv2c GETNEXT requests and RESPONSE PDUs across the MIB-II system group.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, SNMP2, GETNEXT, RESPONSE, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, COMMUNITY, REQID, VARBIND, NULLVAL, STRING, OIDVAL, TIMETICKS, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define a management workstation running snmpwalk with IP 10.121.0.50.
HOST walk_client { IP 10.121.0.50 MAC 00:25:b5:00:21:50 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a switch SNMP agent with IP 10.121.0.1.
HOST walk_target { IP 10.121.0.1 MAC 00:25:b5:00:21:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow walking 1.3.6.1.2.1.1 via three sequential GETNEXT/RESPONSE pairs with incrementing REQIDs.
FLOW snmpv2c_mib_walk(client, agent) {
    client -> agent SNMP2 GETNEXT SRCPORT 53100 DSTPORT 161 COMMUNITY "public" REQID 201 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1 NULLVAL WAIT 5ms
    client <- agent SNMP2 RESPONSE SRCPORT 161 DSTPORT 53100 COMMUNITY "public" REQID 201 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 STRING "Juniper Networks, Inc. ex4300-48t" WAIT 5ms
    client -> agent SNMP2 GETNEXT SRCPORT 53100 DSTPORT 161 COMMUNITY "public" REQID 202 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 NULLVAL WAIT 5ms
    client <- agent SNMP2 RESPONSE SRCPORT 161 DSTPORT 53100 COMMUNITY "public" REQID 202 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0 OIDVAL 1.3.6.1.4.1.2636.1.1.1.2.63 WAIT 5ms
    client -> agent SNMP2 GETNEXT SRCPORT 53100 DSTPORT 161 COMMUNITY "public" REQID 203 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.2.0 NULLVAL WAIT 5ms
    client <- agent SNMP2 RESPONSE SRCPORT 161 DSTPORT 53100 COMMUNITY "public" REQID 203 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0 TIMETICKS 4829100 WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to run the SNMPv2c GETNEXT MIB walk.
COMPILE {
    snmpv2c_mib_walk(walk_client, walk_target)
}
```

```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate an SNMPv2c INFORM notification timeout and retransmission with the same REQID before the NMS returns a RESPONSE acknowledgment.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, SNMP2, INFORM, RESPONSE, SRCPORT, DSTPORT, COMMUNITY, REQID, OID, SYSUPTIME, VARBIND, STRING, INT, WAIT, ms, s, COMPILE

FLOW snmpv2c_inform_retry(router, nms) {
    router -> nms SNMP2 INFORM SRCPORT 58162 DSTPORT 162 COMMUNITY "wan_inform" REQID 8905 OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3 SYSUPTIME 410000 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1.8 INT 8 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.8 STRING "Serial0/1/0" WAIT 2s
    router -> nms SNMP2 INFORM SRCPORT 58162 DSTPORT 162 COMMUNITY "wan_inform" REQID 8905 OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3 SYSUPTIME 410200 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1.8 INT 8 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.8 STRING "Serial0/1/0" WAIT 20ms

### `examples/l7/snmp/snmpv2c/snmpv2c_pdus_over_ipv6.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: SNMPv2c operations over IPv6 covering GET, GETBULK with nonrepeaters, INFORM, and RESPONSE.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, FLOW, ->, <-, SNMP2, GET, GETBULK, NONREPEATERS, MAXREPETITIONS, INFORM, RESPONSE, COMMUNITY, OID, SYSUPTIME, VARBIND, NULLVAL, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define IPv6 SNMPv2c NMS client.
HOST v6_nms { IP 2001:db8:100::1 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define IPv6 SNMPv2c managed agent.
HOST v6_agent { IP 2001:db8:100::2 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define SNMPv2c PDU operations flow.
FLOW snmp2_v6_flow(n, a) {
    n -> a SNMP2 GET COMMUNITY "public" VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0 NULLVAL
    n -> a SNMP2 GETBULK COMMUNITY "public" NONREPEATERS 1 MAXREPETITIONS 10
    n -> a SNMP2 INFORM COMMUNITY "public" OID "1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.3" SYSUPTIME 500
    n <- a SNMP2 RESPONSE COMMUNITY "public"
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block executing SNMPv2c operations over IPv6.
COMPILE {
    snmp2_v6_flow(v6_nms, v6_agent)
}
```

// PROMPT: Simulate periodic 1-second SNMPv2c CPU and memory utilization polling using a LOOP block and WAIT 1s interval.

```fasm
// PROMPT: Demonstrate FrameAssembly OID syntax flexibility using quoted OIDs, unquoted multi-segment OIDs, and 4-segment IPv4-shaped OIDs (1.3.6.1) in OID and OIDVAL fields.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, SNMP2, TRAP, GET, RESPONSE, COMMUNITY, REQID, OID, SYSUPTIME, VARBIND, OIDVAL, STRING, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define an OID syntax test manager with IP 10.132.0.100.
HOST oid_manager { IP 10.132.0.100 MAC 00:11:22:32:00:64 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow mixing quoted OIDs ("1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.1"), unquoted OIDs (1.3.6.1.4.1.8072), and 4-arc OIDs (1.3.6.1).
FLOW oid_format_permutations(agent, manager) {

    agent <- manager SNMP2 GET COMMUNITY "public" REQID 8502 OID 1.3.6.1 WAIT 10ms
    agent -> manager SNMP2 RESPONSE COMMUNITY "public" REQID 8502 VARBIND 1.3.6.1 OIDVAL 1.3.6.1.4.1 WAIT 10ms
}

    oid_format_permutations(oid_agent, oid_manager)
}

// PROMPT: Simulate an SNMPv2c SET request using a read-write community string to administratively disable and re-enable a switch port (ifAdminStatus) with confirmation responses.

    controller <- switch_node SNMP2 RESPONSE SRCPORT 161 DSTPORT 55161 COMMUNITY "private_rw" REQID 4002 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.7.5 INT 1 WAIT 10ms

```fasm
// PROMPT: Generate an RFC 3414 SNMPv3 authPriv TRAP using HMAC-MD5-96 authentication (AUTH MD5) and DES-CBC privacy encryption (PRIV DES).
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, SNMP3, TRAP, USER, ENGINEID, ENGINEBOOTS, ENGINETIME, AUTH, MD5, PRIV, DES, OID, SYSUPTIME, VARBIND, STRING, INT, COMPILE

// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, SNMP3, INFORM, RESPONSE, USER, ENGINEID, ENGINEBOOTS, ENGINETIME, AUTH, SHA, PRIV, AES, REQID, OID, SYSUPTIME, VARBIND, STRING, COUNTER32, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

    sw <- nms SNMP3 RESPONSE USER "usm_sha_aes" ENGINEID "80007571010a950001" ENGINEBOOTS 21 ENGINETIME 105000 AUTH SHA "sha_enterprise_auth" PRIV AES "aes_enterprise_priv" REQID 9501 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.1 STRING "FortyGigE1/0/1" VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.14.1 COUNTER32 29 WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to execute the SHA + AES SNMPv3 INFORM exchange.
COMPILE {
    snmpv3_sha_aes_inform(v3_sha_aes_switch, v3_sha_aes_nms)
}
```

### `examples/l7/snmp/snmpv3/snmpv3_des_padding_boundary_varbinds.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Exercise RFC 3414 DES-CBC zero-padding across different ScopedPDU lengths by sending SNMPv3 PRIV DES packets with varying STRING varbind lengths.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, SNMP3, TRAP, USER, ENGINEID, ENGINEBOOTS, ENGINETIME, AUTH, SHA, PRIV, DES, REQID, OID, SYSUPTIME, VARBIND, STRING, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define an SNMPv3 crypto test agent with IP 10.158.0.5.
HOST des_pad_agent { IP 10.158.0.5 MAC 00:1a:2b:58:00:05 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define an SNMPv3 crypto test receiver with IP 10.158.0.100.
HOST des_pad_receiver { IP 10.158.0.100 MAC 00:1a:2b:58:00:64 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow sending 4 DES-CBC encrypted traps with string varbinds of lengths 1, 4, 8, and 13 bytes to test block alignment.
FLOW des_cbc_padding_vectors(agent, receiver) {
    agent -> receiver SNMP3 TRAP USER "des_tester" ENGINEID "80001f8880580005" ENGINEBOOTS 1 ENGINETIME 100 REQID 10301 AUTH SHA "des_test_auth_123" PRIV DES "des_test_priv_123" OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.1 SYSUPTIME 100 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "A" WAIT 5ms
    agent -> receiver SNMP3 TRAP USER "des_tester" ENGINEID "80001f8880580005" ENGINEBOOTS 1 ENGINETIME 101 REQID 10302 AUTH SHA "des_test_auth_123" PRIV DES "des_test_priv_123" OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.1 SYSUPTIME 101 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "ABCD" WAIT 5ms
    agent -> receiver SNMP3 TRAP USER "des_tester" ENGINEID "80001f8880580005" ENGINEBOOTS 1 ENGINETIME 102 REQID 10303 AUTH SHA "des_test_auth_123" PRIV DES "des_test_priv_123" OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.1 SYSUPTIME 102 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "ABCDEFGH" WAIT 5ms
    agent -> receiver SNMP3 TRAP USER "des_tester" ENGINEID "80001f8880580005" ENGINEBOOTS 1 ENGINETIME 103 REQID 10304 AUTH SHA "des_test_auth_123" PRIV DES "des_test_priv_123" OID 1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5.1 SYSUPTIME 103 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "ABCDEFGHIJKLM" WAIT 5ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to run the DES-CBC block padding test flow.
COMPILE {
    des_cbc_padding_vectors(des_pad_agent, des_pad_receiver)
}
```
### `examples/l7/snmp/snmpv3/snmpv3_engine_discovery_and_time_sync.fasm`
```fasm
// PROMPT: Simulate RFC 3414 SNMPv3 authoritative EngineID discovery and EngineBoots/EngineTime synchronization followed by an authenticated GET/RESPONSE.
// TOKENS: HOST, IP, MAC, FLOW, ->, <-, SNMP3, GET, RESPONSE, USER, ENGINEID, ENGINEBOOTS, ENGINETIME, AUTH, SHA256, PRIV, AES, REQID, VARBIND, NULLVAL, COUNTER32, STRING, WAIT, ms, COMPILE

// INSTRUCTION: Define an NMS discovering a new SNMPv3 agent with IP 10.157.0.10.
HOST discovery_mgr { IP 10.157.0.10 MAC 00:16:3e:57:00:10 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a newly onboarded SNMPv3 router with IP 10.157.0.1.
HOST onboarded_rtr { IP 10.157.0.1 MAC 00:16:3e:57:00:01 }

// INSTRUCTION: Define a flow showing unauthenticated EngineID probe (ENGINEBOOTS 0, ENGINETIME 0), Report response, and synchronized authPriv poll.
FLOW snmpv3_engine_discovery(mgr, rtr) {
    mgr -> rtr SNMP3 GET USER "" ENGINEID "0000000000" ENGINEBOOTS 0 ENGINETIME 0 REQID 10200 WAIT 10ms
    mgr <- rtr SNMP3 RESPONSE USER "" ENGINEID "80001f8880570001" ENGINEBOOTS 0 ENGINETIME 0 REQID 10200 VARBIND 1.3.6.1.6.3.15.1.1.4.0 COUNTER32 1 WAIT 10ms
    mgr -> rtr SNMP3 GET USER "onboard_admin" ENGINEID "80001f8880570001" ENGINEBOOTS 4 ENGINETIME 9200 REQID 10201 AUTH SHA256 "onboard_auth_pass" PRIV AES "onboard_priv_pass" VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 NULLVAL WAIT 10ms
    mgr <- rtr SNMP3 RESPONSE USER "onboard_admin" ENGINEID "80001f8880570001" ENGINEBOOTS 4 ENGINETIME 9200 REQID 10201 AUTH SHA256 "onboard_auth_pass" PRIV AES "onboard_priv_pass" VARBIND 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.5.0 STRING "rtr-onboarded-01" WAIT 10ms
}

// INSTRUCTION: Compile block to run the SNMPv3 engine discovery and synchronization flow.
COMPILE {
    snmpv3_engine_discovery(discovery_mgr, onboarded_rtr)
}
```
